message.content:
A CPU (Central Processing Unit) and a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) are both processors, but they’re designed for different workloads:

| Feature | CPU | GPU |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **Primary purpose** | General‑purpose computing – handles everything from OS tasks to application logic. | Parallel graphics rendering – processes many similar operations simultaneously. |
| **Core count** | Few cores (typically 2–32 in consumer devices). | Hundreds to thousands of smaller cores (e.g., 2,000+ on modern GPUs). |
| **Execution model** | Serial or low‑parallelism; each core can run complex, branching code. | SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data); many cores execute the same instruction stream on different data. |
| **Clock speed** | High clock speeds (≈3–5 GHz) because each core does heavy work. | Lower clock speeds (≈1–1.5 GHz) because many cores share power/thermal budgets. |
| **Cache hierarchy** | Large caches per core (L1/L2/L3) to keep frequently used data close. | Smaller caches per core; relies on massive bandwidth from memory. |
| **Memory access** | Random, high‑latency accesses; CPUs have sophisticated branch prediction and out‑of‑order execution. | Mostly streaming, predictable accesses; GPUs use specialized memory hierarchies (shared memory, texture cache). |
| **Instruction set** | Complex, rich instruction sets (x86, ARM) with many control flow instructions. | Simpler, more uniform instruction sets focused on arithmetic and data movement. |
| **Typical workloads** | Single‑threaded or lightly parallel tasks (web browsing, office apps, OS services). | Highly parallel tasks (graphics rendering, scientific simulations, machine learning inference/training). |
| **Power efficiency** | Optimized for performance per watt in serial workloads. | Optimized for throughput per watt in massively parallel workloads. |

### Why the differences matter

* **Serial vs. Parallel** – CPUs excel at tasks that require complex decision making and low latency. GPUs shine when you can break a problem into thousands of identical, independent operations.
* **Latency vs. Throughput** – CPUs minimize latency for individual operations; GPUs maximize throughput for many operations at once.
* **Flexibility vs. Specialization** – CPUs are generalists; GPUs are specialists optimized for graphics and data‑parallel compute.

In practice, most modern systems use both: the CPU handles the “control plane” (OS, applications, I/O), while the GPU accelerates the “data plane” (graphics, AI, physics). This division lets each processor play to its strengths.
